abstracts.abstract: Complex engineering systems increasingly exhibit multi-dimensional degradation behaviors that cannot be adequately captured by traditional binary-state reliability models. This paper proposes a novel multi-dimensional reliability modeling framework based on stochastic game theory and matrix-based system reliability analysis. The framework characterizes system degradation through state probability vectors across multiple performance dimensions, enabling accurate representation of complex interdependencies among system components. We develop an innovative aggregation algorithm that transforms high-dimensional state spaces into tractable reliability metrics without information loss. The mathematical properties of the framework are rigorously proven, establishing its theoretical foundations. Case studies involving a hybrid electric vehicle powertrain and a spacecraft power distribution system demonstrate the framework's superior capability in capturing subtle degradation patterns that conventional models overlook. The proposed approach reveals failure mechanisms invisible to existing methods, providing more accurate remaining useful life predictions. This work fundamentally reconceptualizes reliability modeling for complex systems by introducing a mathematical paradigm that naturally accommodates multi-dimensional system states. The framework opens new research directions in reliability engineering and provides a rigorous foundation for decision-making in safety-critical applications.

Accurate reliability allocation remains a critical challenge in the design of complex engineering systems, particularly when dealing with imprecise expert knowledge and conflicting design constraints. This paper presents an enhanced multi-objective reliability allocation framework that significantly improves upon existing evidential reasoning approaches. The proposed method incorporates a novel belief structure update mechanism based on generalized information fusion, enabling more effective handling of epistemic uncertainties in expert assessments. We introduce an adaptive weight determination algorithm that dynamically adjusts criteria importance based on system hierarchy and operational profiles. The mathematical properties of convergence and consistency are rigorously established, demonstrating that the improved framework yields more stable and accurate allocation results. Comparative analysis with state-of-the-art methods including TOPSIS and VIKOR variants is conducted across three representative engineering systems: a nuclear reactor cooling system, an aircraft flight control system, and a cloud computing infrastructure. Results consistently show that the proposed framework achieves 15-25% improvement in allocation accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to simpler methods. The framework provides engineering practitioners with a robust tool for reliability allocation under realistic uncertainty conditions.

The proliferation of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems demands fundamentally new approaches to real-time reliability monitoring that traditional centralized architectures cannot provide. This paper presents the design and implementation of a novel edge intelligence-based reliability monitoring system (EdgeRMS) that represents a paradigm shift in how system health is assessed and maintained. The proposed architecture deploys lightweight neural network models directly on edge devices, enabling real-time degradation assessment with millisecond-level latency. A distributed fault detection mechanism coordinates multiple edge nodes through a novel consensus protocol, achieving robust anomaly detection without dependence on cloud connectivity. The system incorporates a physics-informed attention mechanism that seamlessly integrates data-driven learning with first-principles engineering models, addressing the interpretability challenges inherent in black-box approaches. Extensive validation is performed on a water treatment plant testbed and an automotive manufacturing assembly line, demonstrating the system's effectiveness across diverse industrial contexts. The experimental results reveal that EdgeRMS achieves 94.7% fault detection accuracy while reducing communication bandwidth consumption by 78% compared to cloud-based alternatives. This work establishes a new architectural paradigm for reliability engineering in edge-dominated environments.

Existing predictive maintenance systems suffer from significant limitations in handling the complexity and dynamism of modern manufacturing equipment, particularly regarding the integration of heterogeneous sensor data and adaptation to operational context changes. This paper presents an enhanced predictive maintenance framework with substantial improvements in both predictive accuracy and practical deployability. The system architecture integrates a multi-modal feature fusion module that effectively combines vibration, acoustic, thermal, and electrical signals through a novel cross-attention mechanism. We introduce a contextual adaptation layer that dynamically adjusts prediction models based on operating conditions, production schedules, and equipment degradation trajectories. The framework incorporates an uncertainty-aware decision support module that provides maintenance recommendations with quantified confidence intervals, enabling risk-informed planning. Extensive validation on five distinct manufacturing systems—including CNC machines, injection molding equipment, and conveyor systems—demonstrates consistent improvements over existing approaches. The proposed system achieves 12% higher accuracy in remaining useful life prediction and reduces false alarm rates by 31% compared to the baseline. Practical deployment considerations including computational requirements, system integration, and user interface design are thoroughly discussed, providing a complete blueprint for industrial implementation.
